subject: Money
title: SPAC Mania
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on SPAC Mania.

hook.text: In 2021, 613 SPACs raised $162 billion. They were blank-check companies that bought things in the future, maybe.

buildup.text: SPACs let companies go public without the scrutiny of a traditional IPO. Celebrity sponsors added hype.

discovery.text: SPACs could make wild growth projections that regular IPOs couldn't. Future revenue estimates replaced actual earnings.

twist.text: By 2023, most SPAC stocks had lost 50-90% of their value. The sponsors kept their shares; investors took the losses.

climax.text: SPACs weren't innovation—they bypassed rules meant to protect investors. Deregulation disguised as progress.

punchline.text: A blank check. With a prewritten loss.

quiz.question: Why were SPACs attractive to companies going public?
options: Less regulatory scrutiny and the ability to project future revenue
